h2: ECT inspection services in Kansas City: a two-state metro and the tube signals that drive decisions
html:
ECT inspection services in Kansas City: a two-state metro and the tube signals that drive decisions

ECT inspection services in Kansas City are mostly tube examinations on condensers, chillers, process exchangers and boilers, scheduled into plant shutdowns on both sides of the state line. Missouri and Kansas inspect boilers and pressure vessels through different agencies, so the jurisdiction is confirmed for each site. Atlantis selects the tube technique by material, mobilises a crew from Houston and quotes each scope.

Two jurisdictions in one metro. On the Missouri side, the National Board lists the Division of Fire Safety's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Unit; on the Kansas side, the Office of the State Fire Marshal. Radiation licensing splits the same way. Kansas is an NRC Agreement State, so its own program licenses radioactive materials, while Missouri is not, so radiography on the Missouri side is licensed by the NRC through its Region III office. That matters when a tube campaign is paired with radiography of tube-to-tubesheet or nozzle repairs, and the radiography arrangements are confirmed per job.

Reading the signals. Bobbin eddy current gives two kinds of channel. Differential channels respond sharply to pits, cracks and other abrupt changes; absolute channels show gradual wall loss and long-run thinning. Multi-frequency mixes suppress the signals from support plates and baffles so a defect underneath them is not lost. Depth calls come from phase angle against a curve built on the calibration standard, which is why the standard must match the tube exactly and why an analyst's call should be reviewed by a second analyst on the indications that drive plugging.

For carbon-steel tubes, where bobbin eddy current does not penetrate usefully, the plan switches to remote field screening with IRIS ultrasonic sizing on a sample of the worst tubes.

Trending from campaign to campaign. A single ECT campaign tells the owner which tubes to plug now. Two or three campaigns with raw data kept in native format tell the owner how fast the bundle is losing wall and when re-tubing has to be budgeted. Tube identities, row and column numbering and the calibration standard should therefore stay the same between campaigns, and results can be held against the asset in Atlantis ERP asset management so the history does not live in a folder of PDFs.

What the owner decides and what the contractor decides:

  • The contractor examines, analyses and reports each tube's indications against the agreed procedure.
  • The owner's engineer decides plugging, sleeving and re-tubing.
  • For boilers, the commissioned inspector of whichever state holds the equipment decides on the certificate.

The national eddy current testing service lists probe types, third-party inspection in Kansas City covers wider inspection support, and NDT consulting in Missouri covers procedure work. Local technicians can train through NDT training in Kansas City and eddy current testing training. To plan a Kansas City tube campaign, send the bundle details and outage date.
